script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LOS ANGELES COLLEGE - DAY

We open on a vibrant, bustling college campus. Students mill about, chatting and laughing. We see a JV SOCCER TEAM practicing on the field. In the center, JAMES, our protagonist, a talented but misunderstood player, observes from the sidelines. He's alone.

JAMES
(whispering to himself)
Another practice. Another day of being invisible.

Suddenly, a voice behind him.

RACHEL (20s, energetic, confident)
You're not invisible, James. I've seen you. You're incredible.

Startled, James turns around and makes eye contact with RACHEL, the team's star forward.

JAMES
Really? I didn't think you noticed me.

RACHEL
I've noticed how hard you work, even when you're not on the field. I've noticed your determination and your unique playstyle. You're a valuable player, James.

James is shocked. He's never had anyone believe in him like this before.

JAMES
Thank you, Rachel. I really appreciate it.

RACHEL
You're welcome. I want to help you make a difference on the team. Will you join me for lunch after practice?

James hesitates, surprised but excited by the offer.

JAMES
Sure. I'd like that.

INT. COLLEGE CAFETERIA - DAY

James and Rachel sit down at a table, and Rachel starts to ask him about his background and dreams. As they eat, they bond over their shared love for soccer and their desire to make an impact on the team.

RACHEL
So, James, tell me about yourself. Where did you grow up? What got you into soccer?

JAMES
I grew up in a rough neighborhood. Soccer was my escape. I spent hours on the streets playing, just trying to stay out of trouble. My older brother, he's the one who taught me everything I know. He's the reason I love the game so much.

RACHEL
That's amazing. I've always believed soccer has the power to bring people together and change lives. What position do you play?

JAMES
I'm a midfielder. I love controlling the game and setting up my teammates for success.

RACHEL
Midfielders are the heart of the team. You have a special gift, James. I can tell you're going to make a difference here.

James smiles, feeling more appreciated and valued than he ever has before.

JAMES
Thank you, Rachel. I really want to make you proud.

INT. LOS ANGELES COLLEGE - DAY (GYMNASIUM)

James and Rachel are practicing passing drills together. James is making great progress, and Rachel's encouragement and support are helping him believe in himself.

RACHEL
See, James? You've got this. Keep pushing yourself.

As they practice, the team coach, COACH MILLER (40s, stern, but fair) notices their improvement and begins to include James in more scrimmages.

INT. LOS ANGELES COLLEGE - NIGHT

The team gathers in the common room to watch a soccer match on TV. Rachel invites James to join them. They sit together, cheering on their favorite teams and discussing strategies.

RACHEL
James, do you have a favorite team?

JAMES
I do. It's a team from Barcelona. Messi is my favorite player. He's so creative and unpredictable on the field.

RACHEL
You know, James, I think you have that same creativity and unpredictability. You just need to believe in yourself.

INT. LOS ANGELES COLLEGE - DAY (FIELD)

James is given a starting position in the next game. As he steps onto the field, he feels a surge of confidence and determination. He plays with passion and skill, setting up his teammates for goals and making incredible plays of his own.

COACH MILLER (shouting from the sidelines)
Great job, James! Keep it up!

As the game progresses, James and his team start to dominate, and they win the match. James is hailed as a hero, but he knows it's all thanks to Rachel's belief in him.

INT. LOS ANGELES COLLEGE - NIGHT (COMMON ROOM)

The team gathers to celebrate their win. Rachel approaches James, proud of his progress.

RACHEL
James, you were incredible out there today. I knew you could do it.

JAMES
I couldn't have done it without you, Rachel. Your belief in me gave me the courage to believe in myself.

RACHEL
That's what friends are for.

FADE OUT.
